_meta.purpose: Hand-curated address -> semantic-name table for DWARF-nameless game-CU statics (win32_pilot.md task brief, PROMOTIONS.md batch 7, mechanism A). Consumed by carrier/gen/gen_interop.py's collect_globals() (and, by reuse, carrier/gen/gen_src_headers.py's game_state.h/state.c output and carrier/gen/gen_bindings.py's pf_bindings*.h output, since all three walk the SAME globals list gen_interop.py builds) so that a truly nameless static gets a real identifier in the generated headers instead of being silently dropped. The clean SOURCE under src/ never gains a new address literal from this file -- src/ only ever sees the resulting plain name (an ordinary extern), exactly like any DWARF-named global. The address stays recorded ONLY here and in the generated carrier-side headers (it_globals.h/interop_index.json/pf_bindings*.h), per ROADMAP.md SS2's 'clean SOURCE stays address-free' intent.
_meta.purity_gate: src/icytower/names.json is a .json data file. scripts/check_native_layer.py only globs *.c/*.h under src/ (see its `files = ... rglob('*.c') + rglob('*.h')` line), so this file is never scanned and never needs a gate exception -- the addresses it records are data, not code, and they are not reachable from src/ compilation at all (only the generators read this file; src/ itself is never told an address). Decision recorded here rather than editing the gate: keeping the table under src/icytower/ (next to the globals it names) rather than under carrier/gen/ makes it easier to find when investigating a 'why is this global unnamed' question starting from src/, and the purity gate's existing *.c/*.h scope already excludes it without any code change.
_meta.schema: entries live under "globals", keyed by the exact lowercase hex VA gen_interop.py's DWARF walk would have produced (DW_OP_addr, e.g. "0x4dd300"). Each entry: {"name": <C identifier>, "type": <one of gen_interop.py's primitive type spellings, e.g. "int", "unsigned int">, "meaning": <one-line English>, "evidence": <how it was determined -- disassembly VAs, cross-referenced call sites, etc.>}. ONLY add an entry here after confirming (grep artifacts/dwarf_info.txt for the bare hex address, e.g. "grep -n 'DW_OP_addr: 4dd300' artifacts/dwarf_info.txt") that DWARF truly has NO coverage of the address at all -- not as a top-level DW_TAG_variable, and not as a DW_AT_data_member_location offset inside some OTHER already-named global's struct/array type. The second check matters: PROMOTIONS.md batch 7 found that both addresses this table was originally going to carry (0x4dd300, 0x4fabf4/f8/fc) are NOT actually nameless -- 0x4dd300 is sounds[8] (SAMPLE *sounds[9], already in game_state.h) and 0x4fabf4/f8/fc are custom.jump_sound[0..2] (Tcustom.jump_sound[3], already in game_types.h/game_state.h via the `custom` global) -- an earlier pass's 'no DWARF name anywhere' claim only checked for a direct top-level DW_OP_addr match and missed both aggregate-member cases. Re-derive with gen_interop.compute_type_origin-style DWARF member-offset arithmetic (VA - aggregate_base -> DW_AT_data_member_location, or VA - array_base -> element_index * element_size) before concluding an address is genuinely nameless.
_meta.current_status: empty this pass, and PROVEN empty by exhaustive check, not just 'nothing needed yet': a one-off scan (PROMOTIONS.md batch 7) walked every DW_TAG_variable DIE in all 25 game-scope CUs and confirmed there are ZERO with an address (DW_AT_location) but no DW_AT_name -- every game-scope global DWARF describes already has a real name. The two addresses this task's brief cited as 'unnamed globals' (0x4dd300, 0x4fabf4/f8/fc) are not exceptions to that: they are DW_TAG_member offsets inside already-named aggregates (sounds[8] and custom.jump_sound[0..2] respectively), which by construction are never top-level DW_TAG_variable DIEs and so were never candidates for this table in the first place -- an earlier pass's 'no DWARF name anywhere' claim only checked for a literal top-level DW_OP_addr match at the exact computed address and missed the aggregate-member case. The mechanism below (gen_interop.py --names, collect_globals() consulting NAMES_TABLE) is implemented and tested two ways: against the real DWARF, a scratch entry at a nonexistent address is correctly a no-op (156 globals in, 156 out -- collect_globals only ever consults NAMES_TABLE for a DIE it already visited, never invents one); and, since this DWARF has no real nameless DIE to exercise the positive path against, a synthetic-DIE unit test (one hand-built nameless DW_TAG_variable, bypassing parse_dwarf entirely) confirms collect_globals() DOES pick up NAMES_TABLE's name and tags the entry named_via_table=true when a matching DIE exists. Left in place, wired into the generator, for the next pass that finds a genuine one -- outside this DWARF's current game scope, or after a future recompile changes it.
